h1: Fruit of the Loom kids' clothing — sizes by height, models and prices
intro: Fruit of the Loom makes children's T-shirts, hoodies, sweatshirts and sweatpants in the same fabrics as the adult range, at prices that make sense for clothes that will be outgrown in a year. This guide explains the height-based size system, the models sold in Europe and what you should pay in 2026.

body_html:
How do Fruit of the Loom kids' sizes work?

Unlike most high-street children's ranges, Fruit of the Loom does not label kids' clothes by age. Each size is a number that corresponds to the child's height in centimetres. That is deliberate: two seven-year-olds can differ by 15 cm, so height is a far more reliable guide than a birthday.

Measure the child standing against a wall without shoes, then pick the size whose height range includes that number. If the child is at the top of a range — or you want the garment to last a second school year — go one size up.

From about 164 cm most teenagers move into adult XS or S (chest 84–94 cm). The adult chart and measuring instructions are in our {{LINK:size-guide|Fruit of the Loom size guide}}.

Which Fruit of the Loom models are made for kids?

The kids' range mirrors the adult basics, using the same fabrics scaled down. The models you will meet most often in Europe:

Kids Valueweight T (61-033)

The children's version of the best-selling Valueweight T: 100 % ring-spun cotton (heather colours contain polyester), crew neck, regular fit and a smooth surface that prints well. It is the default choice for school events, sports days and everyday wear.

Kids Classic Hooded Sweat (62-043)

A scaled-down Classic Hooded Sweat: 280 g/m² in 80 % cotton / 20 % polyester. The polyester share keeps shrinkage low and the shape stable through the endless washing that children's clothes get. This is the model behind most school-leaver and club hoodies for younger age groups.

Kids crewneck sweatshirt and sweatpants

A kids' crewneck sweatshirt (the hoodless sibling of the Classic Hooded Sweat) and cuffed kids' sweatpants complete the set, so a child can wear a full matching tracksuit for PE, training or the sofa.

Why is Fruit of the Loom so popular for school and club clothing?

Walk past any European primary-school sports day and you will see the brand. Three things explain it:

  • Price — at €4.95 for a T-shirt, a class of 25 can be kitted out for approx. €111 after the 10 % quantity discount, before printing.
  • Consistency — sizes 104 to 164 and the adult XS–3XL share the same colour palette, so teachers, parents and older siblings can wear matching garments.
  • Printability — the same smooth ring-spun cotton as the adult tees takes screen print, DTG and embroidery cleanly, which is why print shops stock it by default.

Ordering for a group? Ask for each child's height rather than age, and add two or three extra pieces in the most common sizes (usually 128 and 140) — those run out first. Our {{LINK:team-hoodies|guide to class and team hoodies}} covers timing, print methods and cost per child.

How should you wash Fruit of the Loom kids' clothes?

Children's clothes are washed more than anything else in the house, so care matters more than for adult basics.

  • Wash at 30–40 °C. Cotton tees can shrink a few per cent on a hot first wash; the 80/20 sweats shrink less.
  • Turn printed garments inside out to protect names, logos and class prints.
  • Air dry or tumble on low — a hot tumble cycle is the main cause of a hoodie that suddenly "got small".
  • Buying a size up for growth is fine on hoodies and sweatpants (the cuffs hold the length in); on T-shirts it looks baggy, so stick to the height chart.

Marmalade Co. shows an OEKO-TEX certificate on its kids' product pages, meaning the fabrics have been tested for harmful substances — reassuring for garments worn next to a child's skin all day.

Which size should you order — a quick decision guide

  • Child is in the middle of a height range: order that size.
  • Child is within 3 cm of the top of a range: order the next size up.
  • Hoodie or sweatpants for winter over other layers: next size up.
  • T-shirt for a one-day event or print: exact size — it looks better in photos.
  • Teenager over 164 cm: switch to adult XS or S and use the chest chart.

faq.q: How do I choose the right Fruit of the Loom kids' size?
faq.a: Measure the child's height in cm and match it to the size number: 104 for 98–104 cm, 116 for 110–116 cm, 128 for 122–128 cm, 140 for 134–140 cm, 152 for 146–152 cm and 164 for 158–164 cm. Ages (3–4 up to 14–15 years) are only a rough guide; height is what the garment is cut for.

faq.q: Which Fruit of the Loom models are available for kids?
faq.a: The core kids' models are the Kids Valueweight T (61-033) in 100 % cotton, the Kids Classic Hooded Sweat (62-043) at 280 g/m² in 80/20 cotton-polyester, a kids' crewneck sweatshirt and cuffed kids' sweatpants. All come in several colours and use the same fabrics as the adult range, scaled down to sizes 104–164.

faq.q: How much does a Fruit of the Loom kids' T-shirt cost?
faq.a: The cheapest verified price is €4.95 incl. VAT at Marmalade Co., with 5 % off for 3 pieces and 10 % off for 5 or more. Marketplaces and print shops usually charge €7–10 for the same blank shirt. Shipping at Marmalade Co. is €7 flat with DHL and takes an estimated 2–3 business days.

faq.q: How much is a Fruit of the Loom kids' hoodie?
faq.a: Marmalade Co. lists the kids' hoodie at €17.95 incl. VAT in black, grey and navy, sizes 116–152, dropping to approx. €16.16 each for 5 or more. Elsewhere in Europe expect €22–28. The hoodie is 280 g/m² in 80 % cotton / 20 % polyester, so it holds its shape well through frequent washing.

faq.q: Is Fruit of the Loom kids' clothing good for printing?
faq.a: Yes. The kids' tees and sweats use the same smooth ring-spun cotton as the adult models, so screen print, DTG and embroidery come out clean. That, plus the low price and matching adult sizes, is why it is the standard choice for class T-shirts, sports clubs and school-leaver hoodies.

faq.q: Does Fruit of the Loom kids' clothing shrink?
faq.a: The 100 % cotton T-shirts can shrink a few per cent on a hot first wash; the 80/20 hoodies and sweatpants shrink less. Wash at 30–40 °C, turn prints inside out and avoid hot tumble drying. If the child is near the top of a height range, order the next size up to allow for growth.
